page: Amazon Web Services m5.16xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the AWS Nitro hypervisor. It features an Intel Xeon 8175M processor with 64 vCPUs, corresponding to 32 physical cores with hyper-threading, running at a clock speed of 3.1 GHz. The system includes 256.0 GB of DDR4 memory operating at 3 GHz, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per vCPU. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, relying entirely on network-attached storage. Network connectivity is supported by a 20 Gbps baseline bandwidth.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by stress-ng and Geekbench single-core scores falling in the bottom 25%. However, the 64 vCPUs deliver average multi-core performance, with stress-ng multi-core, PassMark CPU, and Geekbench multi-core scores landing in the middle 50%. Notably, memory bandwidth for large uncached blocks is strong, reaching 192.72 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25%, while small-block read and large-block write bandwidths remain average.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the m5.16xlarge is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads that scale horizontally across many threads rather than relying on high single-thread performance. It is well-suited for multi-threaded applications, database operations, static web serving, and medium-sized LLM prompt processing, where its average multi-core and strong large-block memory read bandwidth can be leveraged. It is less optimal for single-threaded tasks or large-scale LLM text generation due to weaker single-core and text generation benchmark results.
